payload.headline: The 12th PII carrier was in the TRANSPORT dimension: a privacy boundary that governs a response's CONTENTS governs nothing about its AUDIENCE.
payload.context: Any server-rendered app that personalizes a response (an account menu, a session-derived asset) and serves it with a shared-cacheable cache-control. VEILOS had nine such routes and ZERO Vary headers repo-wide, confirmed live on production behind Cloudflare.
payload.problem: The application-layer boundary can be perfectly correct and still be defeated by the transport layer. S227/S228 had deliberately revoked a raw ?id= as a public render key ('a third party probing a raw id reads exactly what a nonexistent one reads: nothing'). A shared cache handed that revoked capability straight back requiring NO id at all: /passport/card.svg carries no actor in its URL but resolves one from the session, so a CDN keys on the URL alone, stores the first response, and replays one user's proof card to every later caller for the whole TTL.
payload.solution: Bind the audience at the outermost response chokepoint and DERIVE the signal from the request rather than declaring it per-route (declaring at N call sites is instance-binding; the N+1th surface forgets). Rule in two halves: (1) any shared-cacheable response gets Vary: cookie — anonymous callers send no Cookie header so they still share ONE cache entry and lose nothing; (2) a request that CARRIED a cookie has `public` rewritten to `private`. Half (2) is load-bearing, not belt-and-braces: Cloudflare below Enterprise honours Vary only for Accept-Encoding and otherwise caches by URL. Exempt responses that declare `immutable` — a caller-varying body cannot honestly claim it — so static assets keep full edge caching and the guard discriminates instead of blanket-narrowing.
payload.second_order: A guard that needs TWO callers cannot be built from one. A route-parity sentinel that drives a single anonymous request per route is structurally blind to a leak that exists only BETWEEN callers. When building the two-caller sweep, subtract each route's own non-determinism twice (normalize timestamps AND require two identical anonymous calls to agree) — our first measurement produced three false positives from millisecond `generated_at` stamps, and shipping that would have produced a sentinel that reds forever on innocent routes and gets ignored within a session.
payload.second_lesson: A derived field with a mechanical prover needs a PROVENANCE check, not just a consistency check. Our deploy receipt had a correct recorder that the previous closeout simply bypassed by hand — leaving main RED and publishing a false deploy state to the studio's machine-readable source of truth. Because the prover is a pure function its emittable set is enumerable, so 'could this value have come from the prover?' is a real testable question, and it catches the plausible hand edit that internal consistency passes.
payload.applies_to: every studio project serving personalized server-rendered responses or session-derived assets behind a CDN

payload.pattern: An aggregator that reads its child checks through the EXIT CODE alone has a two-state channel (pass / not-pass). The moment any child is a three-state gauge whose honest-absent verdict correctly exits 0 — UNMEASURED, could-not-look, offline, no-data — the aggregator records it as a measured pass. Absence is laundered into proof at the rollup, and every per-gauge honesty cure you already shipped is silently undone one level up. Obelisk proved it in one command: with its network gates blinded, ops-doctor printed 100/100 HEALTHY, 0 blocking, 0 advisory — byte-identical to a fully-measured run. The sharpest case was a WEIGHTED gate scoring full marks for judging nothing, which then let the SIL evidence ceiling leave a category uncapped on a plane nobody had checked.
payload.solution: Make MEASUREMENT an explicitly-declared property, never inferred. (1) A tiny primitive: gates call emitUnmeasured(reason) — reason MANDATORY — beside their existing output; aggregators call a PURE parseGateMeasurement(output, code). (2) Do NOT re-code exit semantics to add a state — UNMEASURED is genuinely not a failure, and re-coding breaks every CLI contract for nothing; put the signal on a channel the reader already captures (stdout). (3) A non-zero exit can NEVER be excused as darkness — that invariant stops the primitive becoming a way to launder a failure. (4) An unmeasured member leaves BOTH the numerator and the denominator, and the shrink is DISCLOSED wherever the score is quoted — awarding the weight and punishing it are equally dishonest. (5) Separate momentary darkness from persistent blindness over a run-window ledger (LIVE/DARK/BLIND, with a minimum-observations floor) or the cure becomes an over-detector that turns yellow on every offline laptop and gets ignored. (6) Enforce the contract in BOTH directions — a gate that CAN go dark but does not declare it is MUTE and fails — or the next check anyone writes silently reintroduces the defect. (7) Carry the darkness count to the surface the founder actually reads; a health tick over gates nobody looked at is the whole lie in miniature. Two sibling findings shared the spine: a CI failure classifier that conflated a conditionally-SKIPPED job with a runner-starved one (making cause=code unreachable on that repo forever), and a blocker detector that asked is-this-human-only but never is-the-premise-still-true, leaving two founder blockers phantom-OPEN for weeks after their reasons had evaporated.

payload.pattern: A span-keyed relationship table silently over-attributes when you sum per-period values across the span
payload.context: franchise-careers.json records a player stint as (first,last) only. Summing per-season value across that span credits a club for seasons the player spent elsewhere inside it — the error is invisible because every number looks plausible.
payload.solution: Attribute a period to an entity ONLY when exactly one entity span covers it. Periods covered by two or more spans are AMBIGUOUS: exclude them from every entity total and PUBLISH the excluded count per entity. Under-crediting is recoverable; a fabricated total is not. In StatVault S248 this credited 3,600 seasons and left 1,258 contested ones with nobody, and the gate proves the property.

payload.pattern: A GitHub Actions workflow can be permanently unrunnable and nothing tells you — invalid YAML just never fires
payload.context: statvault typed-routes-watch.yml used `gh pr create --body "$(cat <<PRBODY" with the heredoc body starting at column 0 INSIDE a `run: |` block. Column 0 ends the block scalar, so the file was not valid YAML. GitHub does not surface a parse failure as a red run — the workflow simply never appears. It sat broken through many sessions because nothing in the repo parsed workflow files.
payload.solution: Add a gate that (a) yaml.load()s every .github/workflows/*.y?ml and (b) asserts each declares at least one trigger. Two traps: bare `on:` parses as the BOOLEAN true in YAML 1.1, so check doc.on ?? doc.true or you will think every workflow has no triggers; and keep any policy scan (e.g. no-hosted-cron) LINE-BASED rather than YAML-based, so a file that fails the parse check is still audited — otherwise a parse error becomes a way to smuggle a cron past the gate. For heredocs in run blocks, write the body with printf to a file and pass --body-file.

payload.pattern: A gate whose resolved authority may live in an UNTRACKED file asks a different question on your machine than in a clean checkout — and the local answer is the one that gets read.
payload.context: Obelisk W229. check-brief-correspondence resolves a test count cache-first from a gitignored file that is ALSO the value's producer, so locally the cache both produced the rendered number and won the ownership resolution. The gate compared the brief against its own source: coherence, not correspondence, inside the very file built to escape that trap. Green three local runs, RED in CI on the same commit. The gate had even NAMED the divergence as a deliberate non-fatal advisory — reasoning that is right about the artifact and blind about the commit. The missing axis was never severity; it was WHICH TREE the question is asked of.
payload.solution: 1) Any check whose owner resolution can reach a gitignored/untracked path must be evaluated on TWO planes: LOCAL (working tree as-is) and PORTABLE (working tree as git sees it — a read of an untracked path returns ABSENT). A fact that corresponds LOCAL and conflicts PORTABLE is the defect. 2) The portable plane is TRACKED-FILES-AT-CURRENT-CONTENT, not HEAD: the question is what a clean checkout of the commit you are ABOUT to make will see — which also catches, for free, a file you created and never git-added. 3) The tracked-set must be null, NEVER an empty set, when git cannot answer; an empty set makes the portable plane see an empty repo and pass everything vacuously. 4) A measurement must land in a TRACKED artifact — writing only to a cache relocates the contradiction past the commit boundary where only CI can see it. 5) MEASURE the gate population instead of declaring it: run the standing suite in a tracked-files-only mirror and diff per-gate verdicts. This disproved our own follow-on item (8 other cache-reading gates did not diverge — reading an untracked path is not the defect, RESTING A VERDICT on one is). 6) PASS-here/DEGRADED-there is darkness, not a scheduled failure — scoring it fatal makes the harness an over-detector. 7) The enforcement-parity ratio (how many gates measure in a clean checkout) is a number worth having: ours is 39/40.
payload.applicability: Any repo whose local gates read gitignored caches, .env-derived state, sibling-repo paths, or generated artifacts — i.e. most Studio repos. The tell is a gate that has never failed locally but has failed in CI.
